---
title: "Mathematics and Computing for Digital Games"
toc: false
format: lesson-html
---

This course develops the mathematics that every game engine computes many
times per second: coordinate systems, vectors and matrices, geometric
transformations (translation, rotation and scaling), trigonometry, probability
and random numbers, and mathematical logic. Each concept is introduced through
a game situation, formalised, worked through with examples, and then applied to
problems from game development.

**Textbook.** Dunn, F. and Parberry, I. *3D Math Primer for Graphics and Game
Development*, 2nd ed., CRC Press, 2011. The lesson notes (PDF) follow the order
of the syllabus and refer to the textbook for further reading.

**How to study each lesson.** Read the lesson notes (PDF) before and after the
lecture. Use the interactive lesson page to practise: it has questions with
instant feedback, simulators and mini-games (the PDF links to them with QR
codes). The slides are a short summary for revision.

## Lectures

Lectures of 90 minutes, in teaching order, with a homework after every two lectures. Faded lectures are not available yet.
